848de7371104decdd0c19a77f65d193d88f4345a.summary: GreyNoise tracks GT13, an intrusion campaign against Check Point Security Management Servers with confirmed activity from October 17th to November 2nd, 2026, and at least 22 victim organisations across many countries and sectors. The actor forged admin sessions on an HFS server, built a relay box, and used several CVEs, including a Check Point SmartConsole auth bypass. GreyNoise does not attribute GT13 to any known group and suspects AI-assisted tooling.

hedges: GreyNoise does not attribute GT13 to any known or publicly tracked threat group at this time.
GreyNoise lacks enough information to assess the actor's motivation or nation of origin.
GreyNoise believes the actor used LLMs and agentic systems and suspects a mature AI-enabled offensive apparatus.
GreyNoise expects the campaign is ongoing given persistent access to victim devices; its visibility stopped around November 2nd, 2026.
GreyNoise could not determine when or how the actor first gained access to the Check Point assets.
Time-zone patterns are not weighted heavily; some timeline oddities may reflect agentic offensive operations.
Some egress IP attributions are inferred from a /24 range, and the bulk certificate task was not seen being sent by the actor.
One error message may indicate an implant; the report presents this only as possible.

84479097058c0c9942a1c58a7e814ca2090bdb67.summary: Avast Threat Labs reports that the Lazarus Group exploited a zero-day (CVE-2024-21338) in the Windows AppLocker driver appid.sys to gain kernel read/write access, then ran an updated FudModule rootkit. The rootkit uses nine techniques, four of them new, and targets security software including Microsoft Defender, CrowdStrike Falcon and HitmanPro. Microsoft patched the flaw in its February Patch Tuesday update. The rootkit is data-only and the report says it remains under active development. A new RAT attributed to Lazarus is to be covered in a planned follow-up.

hedges: The report says it can only speculate on Lazarus's motivation for choosing the zero-day approach over BYOVD, and believes stealth was the primary motive.
The report says the actual impact of one rootkit technique remains unclear because it did not reverse engineer a competitor's product.
The report says the vulnerability may only barely meet Microsoft's security servicing criteria.
The report says the dropped status file is presumably inspected through hands-on keyboard activity via a RAT command.
The report says the most likely explanation for the image verification technique is that the actors are preparing to load a malicious driver later.
The report says the Korean origin of the debug strings is only a supposed origin, based on language analysis.
The report says the RAT technical details and initial infection vector are to be published in a follow-up post.
